genesis.16.p1.b1.text: Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.

genesis.16.p1.b2.text: “Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.”

genesis.16.p1.b3.text: So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.

genesis.16.p2.b4.text: … she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.

genesis.16.p2.b5.text: “May the wrong done to me be upon you! … ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”

genesis.16.p2.b6.text: “… your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.”

genesis.16.p2.b7.text: Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.

genesis.16.p3.b8.text: Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert—the spring along the road to Shur.

genesis.16.p3.b9.text: “Hagar, servant of Sarai … where have you come from, and where are you going?”

genesis.16.p3.b10.text: “I am running away from my mistress Sarai …”

genesis.16.p3.b11.text: “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.” … “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”

genesis.16.p4.b12.text: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.

genesis.16.p4.b13.text: He will be a wild donkey of a man … he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.”

genesis.16.p4.b14.text: So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me” …

genesis.16.p4.b15.text: “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”

genesis.16.p5.b16.text: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.

genesis.16.p5.b17.text: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
